name: Feature-grid-lockup
purpose: A marketing feature grid: N cells of icon + title + body, arranged 2/3/4-up. Composed from the gated Cards atom's Action-card icon/title/body geometry (its per-cell action-button row deliberately omitted — a feature-grid cell states a benefit, it does not carry its own call to action) plus 4 byte-matched library icons. Wave-6 itinerary row 123 (Layer 2, class NO-ARTEFACT-CLASS at mint; PROPOSED here, not ruled).

props.name: density
props.$note: Three arrangement variants drawn in the reference: A 2-up, B 3-up, C 4-up. Structural variance (cell count and minimum track width), a VARIANTS-axis prop.

props.name: cells
props.$note: Each cell is an icon + a t-cm-button title + a t-ed-body-small body line. The specimen shows 2-4 cells per density; nothing in the grid caps the count beyond what the density's own minmax track implies.

variants.name: up-2
variants.use: A focused pair of benefits — the widest cell, for when only two things matter.

variants.name: up-3
variants.use: The most common marketing density — three benefits, still legible at a glance.

variants.name: up-4
variants.use: A dense capability list — the narrowest cell, for a longer feature set.

tokens.cell: tertiary/background/default + border/subtle + border-radius/surface, via Cards.reference.html's `.card` base, unmodified
tokens.icon: icon/default, via Cards.reference.html's Action-card icon slot, unmodified
tokens.title: borrowed from canon/type.css .t-cm-button composite (16px/500) — the EXACT match to Cards' own raw h3 declaration, never re-declared raw here
tokens.body: borrowed from canon/type.css .t-ed-body-small composite (14px/400) — the EXACT match to Cards' own raw p declaration, never re-declared raw here
tokens.$note: Every token above resolves through the ATOM's own manifest or the type-composite ramp; this organism binds nothing new. The lock-up's own CSS (`.fgl-*`) is grid arrangement only — no colour, no type-size, no radius declaration of its own.

$icons.$note: All 4 byte-matched from the icon library (lesson 4) — verified against `_ICON-SOURCE-AUDIT.md`: Feature-grid-lockup 4/4 verified, 0 bespoke, 0 unknown.

responsive.$status: PROPOSED at #210 wave-6 (not ruled) — reflow verified in a real browser at 3 widths.
responsive.rule: Each density's own auto-fit minmax track (300/240/200px) reflows the column count as the container narrows. A second, explicit rule collapses ALL densities to one column under a 480px container — the floor beneath the auto-fit floor, so a 2-up grid in a genuinely narrow panel never sits at an awkward two-column squeeze before it gives up and stacks.
responsive.$note: s210-D3 discipline: the lock-up declares no width of its own; the container gives it one. ★ CONTAINER-QUERY SELF-QUERY TRAP AVOIDED (wave-5 lesson 3): `.fgl-outer` (the ancestor) carries `container-type:inline-size`; the `@container` rule targets `.fgl-grid`, its DESCENDANT, never the container itself.

accessibility.structure: Each cell is an <article> with a single heading; icons are aria-hidden decorative marks alongside a text title, never the only signal of what the cell is about.
accessibility.colourIsNeverAlone: No RAG value appears anywhere in this component.

antiPatterns: Re-drawing the card CSS instead of composing the existing Cards atom
Giving the lock-up a fixed width — s210-D3 reserves that for the container
Adding a per-cell button — that re-introduces Cards' Action-card `.actions` row, which this lock-up deliberately omits; a per-cell CTA is CTA-lockup's job, not this one's
Putting the container-query rule on the same element it collapses — the wave-5 self-query trap; the ancestor (`.fgl-outer`) must be the container, never `.fgl-grid` itself
